title: Questions and Answers: NDMA impurities in metformin products
journal: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Safety and Availability, content current as of 3 September 2020
result: FDA recommended recalls of certain metformin products that may contain N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) above the acceptable intake limit, and asked five manufacturers of extended-release metformin to recall lots. Its testing found elevated NDMA in some extended-release formulations but not in the immediate-release formulation or in the active pharmaceutical ingredient, and the agency stated it does not believe the active ingredient is a primary source and was investigating the root cause. All manufacturers of extended-release versions were asked to evaluate their risk of excessive NDMA and to test at-risk product before each batch is released, withholding batches above the limit. FDA stated it does not expect nitrosamines to cause harm when ingested at or below the acceptable intake limit, that impurities may increase cancer risk when exposure exceeds that limit over long periods, that it does not know how long patients may have been exposed to higher levels, and that it does not anticipate shorter-term exposure above the limit to increase cancer risk. Patients taking recalled metformin were told to continue it until a clinician or pharmacist provided a replacement, because stopping without advice could be dangerous in type 2 diabetes.
